MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for FKRP-related muscular dystrophy. Clinical suspicion of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy or congenital muscular dystrophy based on patient presentation.

METHODOLOGY
Targeted DNA sequencing of the FKRP gene (NM_024301.5) was performed. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes. All coding exons and flanking intronic sequences of the FKRP gene were amplified by PCR and analyzed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing. This assay detects point mutations and small insertions/deletions within the coding regions and splice sites. Large deletions/duplications are not detected by this methodology.

RESULTS
Gene: FKRP (Fukutin-related protein)
Reference Sequence: NM_024301.5

Variant Detected:
c.826C>A (p.Leu276Ile)
Zygosity: Homozygous
Classification: Likely Pathogenic

This variant results in a leucine to isoleucine substitution at codon 276 of the FKRP protein. The c.826C>A (p.Leu276Ile) variant is the most common pathogenic variant identified in patients with LGMD2I (Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy type 2I) and has been reported in multiple affected individuals in the literature. This variant has been shown to result in reduced α-dystroglycan glycosylation, which is the underlying molecular defect in FKRP-related muscular dystrophies.

SUMMARY
Molecular genetic testing identified a homozygous likely pathogenic variant in the FKRP gene, confirming the clinical diagnosis of FKRP-related muscular dystrophy. The c.826C>A (p.Leu276Ile) variant is associated with a spectrum of phenotypes ranging from mild limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD2I/LGMDR9) to more severe congenital muscular dystrophy (MDC1C). The homozygous state of this common variant is typically associated with the milder LGMD2I phenotype, though clinical severity can vary.

TECHNICAL NOTES
- Coverage: All coding exons achieved minimum 30x coverage
- Quality metrics: Q30 >95%
- This test was developed and validated by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory
- Variant nomenclature follows HGVS guidelines
- Reference genome: GRCh38/hg38

LIMITATIONS
This test does not detect large deletions/duplications, deep intronic variants, or variants in regulatory regions. Rare polymorphisms may interfere with primer binding resulting in allele dropout. A negative result does not exclude the diagnosis of muscular dystrophy.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
